_meta.whatsNew: Adds 6 new origins (Ghana, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Egypt, Sri Lanka, Nepal) to the 4 proven ones (Pakistan, Nigeria, India, Philippines) = 10 nursing→UK corridors. Same UK sharedDestination block (built + validated in v2). Each new corridor carries real cited origin facts with a 'sources' array + 'corroborated' flag, same bar CC's gate enforces (≥1 official OR ≥2 independent).
_meta.CORRECTION_3_sife: IMPORTANT — corrects an overstatement in v2. v2's englishRoute said the 'taught and examined in English' route 'also requires UK-employer SIFE'. That is NOT accurate per the NMC's own pages (surfaced by the Ghana research pass reading nmc.org.uk directly). The NMC offers THREE INDEPENDENT English-evidence routes: (1) accepted test OET/IELTS; (2) one year recent practice in a country on the NMC majority-English list; (3) a pre-registration qualification TAUGHT AND EXAMINED IN ENGLISH, evidenced by institutional transcript/letter + clinical-interaction thresholds. SIFE (Supporting Information From Employers) is a SEPARATE supplementary route used ALONGSIDE other evidence for people who narrowly missed a test or did an English-taught programme abroad and have ~12 months in a UK role — it is NOT a mandatory add-on to route (3). The shared NMC English mechanics now live ONCE in sharedDestination.englishRoutesMechanics; each corridor carries only its origin-distinct nuance (on the majority list? English-medium training?). The honest practical point stays: none of these 10 origins is on the majority-English list, so most applicants still take OET or IELTS — but that is a practical tendency, not an NMC rule, and 'you must have SIFE' is not stated as fact anywhere.
_meta.CORRECTION_carryover: v2 already corrected: (1) the false 'Nigeria/Philippines are exempt' binary — no origin here has an automatic exemption; (2) Philippines authentication is APOSTILLE (red ribbon abolished 2019). Both retained in v3.
_meta.attestationSplit: A genuinely origin-distinct axis: Hague Apostille members among these 10 = Pakistan (in force Mar 2023), India, Philippines (2019) → APOSTILLE, no further UK legalisation. NON-members = Ghana, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Egypt, Sri Lanka, Nepal → full CONSULAR LEGALISATION via each country's foreign ministry. This split is real, sourced (HCCH status table), and distinct per corridor.
_meta.compose_instruction_for_CC: Body of each corridor = origin-distinct facts (originRegulator, verificationRoute, attestationChain, origin fees, englishRoute nuance, localSearchWording). SHARED destination facts (Test of Competence, English routes mechanics + test scores, £ fees, majority-English list) render ONCE on /register/uk-nmc and are LINKED from each corridor — do NOT repeat per corridor (law #3). Load-bearing facts (originRegulator, verificationRoute, attestationChain) use the 'sources' array; the currency gate's corroboration rule applies (≥1 official OR ≥2 independent hosts). feesTimeline is non-blocking, render as 'reported'. Every page keeps the permanent 'confirm current details with the NMC and your national council' caveat + lastVerified. Re-run corridor-report + sitemap-eligibility and report by STATE.

sharedDestination.note: SHARED across all corridors — render once on /register/uk-nmc, link from each corridor. Do NOT repeat per corridor (law #3).

testOfCompetence.value: Overseas-trained nurses must pass the NMC Test of Competence: Part 1 CBT (computer-based test — Part A numeracy, Part B clinical; can be taken in-country) and Part 2 OSCE (objective structured clinical examination, taken at a UK test centre). Both parts within two years of each other.

englishRoutesMechanics.value: The NMC accepts English evidence by ONE of three independent routes: (1) an accepted test — OET (Listening/Reading/Speaking grade B, Writing C+) or IELTS Academic (Listening/Reading/Speaking 7.0, Writing 6.5), within 2 years; two sittings of the SAME test combinable within 12 months (IELTS and OET cannot be mixed); (2) one year's recent practice in a country on the NMC's majority-English-speaking list; or (3) a pre-registration nursing qualification TAUGHT AND EXAMINED IN ENGLISH, evidenced by a transcript/official letter from the training institution PLUS evidence that clinical practice met the NMC's interaction thresholds (a substantial share of practice involving patient interaction, most of it in English). SIFE (Supporting Information From Employers) is a SEPARATE supplementary route — a reference from a CURRENT UK employer, for applicants who narrowly missed a test score or completed an English-taught programme in a non-majority-English country and have ~12 months in a UK health/care role — used only ALONGSIDE other evidence, never alone, and NOT a mandatory add-on to route (3).

nmcFees.value: NMC fee components (subject to change — verify current amounts): qualification/eligibility evaluation £140 (non-refundable), CBT £83, OSCE £794, initial registration £153.

englishMajorityCountryList.value: The NMC's 'recent practice in a majority-English country' route relies on a published list of ~30–34 majority-English-speaking territories (e.g. UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, USA, Jamaica, several Caribbean states). NONE of the 10 origins in this batch (Pakistan, Nigeria, India, Philippines, Ghana, Kenya, Zimbabwe, Egypt, Sri Lanka, Nepal) is on it — so route (2) is not available to them based on home-country practice.

originRegulator.value: Pakistan Nursing & Midwifery Council (PNMC) — reconstituted/renamed from the former Pakistan Nursing Council (PNC).
originRegulator.note: Confirm current legally operative name/portal — pnmc.gov.pk uses the new name; older pnc.org.pk still resolves.

verificationRoute.value: Verification of registration / good standing is obtained directly from PNMC: submit the verification application form, processing fee PKR 10,000, a request letter from the receiving regulator (the UK NMC) with full contact details, and photocopies of the PNMC registration card plus all nursing/midwifery diplomas and degrees. Queries go to the Good Standing Cell (gsc@pnmc.gov.pk). A manual/email-based process, not a self-service outbound portal.

attestationChain.value: Degree attestation via the Higher Education Commission (HEC); school/intermediate certificates countersigned by the IBCC; then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA). Pakistan acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 9 March 2023), so MOFA now issues Apostilles (apostille.mofa.gov.pk) — HEC/IBCC verification remains the prerequisite before the MOFA apostille.

originRegulator.value: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN). Main site nmcn.gov.ng; applicant portal myportal.nmcn.gov.ng; verification info nmcn.gov.ng/verify.html. Payments via REMITA.

verificationRoute.value: The nurse uses NMCN's 'Verification of Certificate' service: apply online on the Council's portal, upload a scanned Certificate(s) of Registration and a passport photo, complete the verification form (destination = UK NMC), pay via REMITA. Only Certificate(s) of Registration are accepted (not exam-result/notification docs). NMCN sends the verification directly to the destination regulator.

verificationEligibilityFeesTimeline.value: Revised NMCN verification guidelines (reported effective 1 March 2024): typically ~2 years post-qualification experience and an active practising licence; NMCN contacts the training institution and workplace directly; allow ~6 months. Fees (via REMITA) reported around: standard verification ≈₦66,875, a UK-specific verification line ≈₦17,500, authentication ≈₦8,750, Letter of Good Standing ≈₦8,750.

englishRoute.value: Nigeria is not on the NMC majority-English list, so route (2) is unavailable from Nigeria. Nigerian pre-registration nursing IS taught and examined in English, so route (3) may be available with institutional evidence and the interaction thresholds met — but even so, applying from Nigeria most nurses still take OET or IELTS. There is no automatic exemption; the belief that Nigerian nurses skip the test is a misconception.

originRegulator.value: Indian Nursing Council (INC) sets national standards and runs the national live register (NRTS), but individual registration is held at the STATE Nursing Council level (constituted under the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947).

verificationRoute.value: India-distinct federal wrinkle: verification of registration / good standing for going abroad is issued by the STATE Nursing Council of first registration (e.g. Tamil Nadu TNMC, Kerala KNMC, Karnataka KSNC, Delhi DNC, Maharashtra MNC) — NOT the Indian Nursing Council. The state council completes its section of the destination regulator's verification form and sends/couriers it directly to that regulator; the applicant supplies passport, registration certificate, experience proof and the destination authority's courier address. Some councils (e.g. Karnataka) include a video verification appointment.

attestationChain.value: For Indian nursing/educational documents used in the UK: authenticated at the State level (Home Department / HRD / SDM), then APOSTILLED by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA). Because India and the UK are both parties to the Hague Apostille Convention, an MEA apostille needs no further UK embassy legalisation. State nursing-council verification is a separate step from document apostille.

originRegulator.value: Professional Regulation Commission (PRC), acting through the Professional Regulatory Board of Nursing. PRC issues the Certificate of Registration (COR) and Professional Identification Card (PIC), and provides certification/authentication and stateboard verification services. Online system: LERIS.

verificationRoute.value: Filipino nurse obtains PRC-authenticated documents via LERIS: log in, book an appointment and pay, present the system-generated Action Sheet plus requirements (valid PIC/e-PIC, originals, one Documentary Stamp Tax per copy). PRC also lists a 'Stateboard Verification / Validation of Registration/License' service used by professionals going abroad. The PRC page does not describe direct electronic transmission to the UK NMC; third-party verifiers (e.g. TruMerit/CGFNS, DataFlow) are commonly used — confirm the exact PRC→NMC handoff.

attestationChain.value: The Philippines abolished the DFA 'red ribbon' and acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force 14 May 2019; embassies stopped red ribbons 15 June 2019). Documents are now APOSTILLED by the DFA: regular PHP 100 (~5 working days) or expedited PHP 200 (~2 working days); appointments at apostille.gov.ph. Because the UK is an Apostille state, an apostilled Philippine document needs no further UK legalisation.
attestationChain.sourceName: Philippine DFA — PH does away with red ribbons

englishRoute.value: Philippines is not on the NMC majority-English list, so route (2) is unavailable from the Philippines. Philippine pre-registration nursing IS taught and examined in English, so route (3) may be available with institutional evidence and the interaction thresholds met — even so, most Filipino nurses applying from home take OET or IELTS. No automatic exemption.

originRegulator.value: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana (NMC Ghana), the statutory body that registers and licenses Nurse Assistants, Nurses and Midwives in Ghana. Note the name collision: the UK regulator is also 'Nursing and Midwifery Council' — they are different bodies (Ghana: nmc.gov.gh; UK: nmc.org.uk).

verificationRoute.value: NMC Ghana operates a Verification / Foreign Verification service (a good-standing / verification-of-registration route) for Ghana-registered practitioners applying to overseas boards such as the UK NMC. The practitioner's PIN must be current (annual renewal with CPD) before verification can be requested; applications are handled through NMC Ghana regional offices, with a 'Foreign Verification Steps' guide on the official site. Confirm the exact fee, timeline and whether NMC Ghana transmits directly to the UK NMC (that direct-send detail is single-secondary) with NMC Ghana (info@nmc.gov.gh).

attestationChain.value: Ghana is NOT a party to the Hague Apostille Convention (confirmed absent from the HCCH status table), so documents cannot be apostilled and require full consular LEGALISATION: Ghanaian public documents (educational/professional) are first authenticated by Ghana's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration (Accra), then legalised by the relevant diplomatic mission. Confirm the exact final UK-facing mission step (British High Commission Accra vs Ghana High Commission London). originRegulator.value: Nursing in Egypt is regulated jointly by the Egyptian Nursing Syndicate (statutory professional body under Law 115 of 1976, maintaining the official register/membership card) and the Ministry of Health and Population (MoHP), which issues/renews the practising licence. For working abroad, good-standing/registration proof comes from these bodies.

verificationRoute.value: There is no single automated regulator-to-regulator verification for Egypt. The nurse applies directly to the UK NMC via the 'trained outside the UK' route (self-assessment, qualification + ID verification, English, Test of Competence CBT+OSCE, health & character, indemnity), and supplies evidence of registration/good standing obtained from the Egyptian Nursing Syndicate / MoHP and legalised (see attestation). The NMC assesses whether the Egyptian qualification/registration is comparable.
